newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KAL targets ex-Denver beef air exports.
newsitem.headline: KAL targets ex-Denver beef air exports.

text.p: Korean Air (KAL ) is targetting U.S. beef exports to fill belly cargo space when it begins three times weekly passenger flights between Seoul and Denver via Los Angeles on May 23, KAL's cargo vice-president and general manager, Ji Young Lee said.
Denver is the South Korean flag carrier's 12th U.S. destination and is now KAL's number one cargo market, Lee added in an interview with Reuters.
He expects to increase cargo capacity to the new U.S. gateway later this year, replacing Boeing 747-400 all-passenger aircraft on Wednesday, Friday and Sundays ex Denver with a Boeing 747 Combi.
"I think we can enjoy step by step development of the cargo market out of Denver first with lower deck capacity then Combi, although I don't think the market is ready for a full freighter," Lee said.
KAL said it was enjoying strong passenger demand for the soon to be launched service but Lee said he expects a directional imbalance for cargo with higher demand for ex-Denver cargo space.
Because he used to work in KAL's Los Angeles regional headquarters, Lee said he had personally surveyed the Denver market three times and spotted potential markets.

"We think there is not bad cargo demand, especially for perishables such as frozen or chilled beef. There is also a large amount of electronic goods made in Colorado with big corporations such as Intel Corp and AT&T having production lines there," Lee added.

Most beef is currently trucked to Los Angeles or San Francisco for shipment by sea to Japan,and Lee said he thought KAL Cargo could win a share of this beef traffic, including that already carried by United Airlines. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
